title: When I need to check inventory levels at the end of the week, I want to automatically reconcile Shop
job_to_be_done: When I need to check inventory levels at the end of the week, I want to automatically reconcile Shopify sales with my warehouse management system, so I can avoid stockouts, overselling, and 4-5 hours of manual spreadsheet work.
painful_workflow: Downloading inventory reports from Shopify and WMS, pasting into Google Sheets, manually comparing SKU counts, and flagging discrepancies.
current_workaround: Download inventory reports from Shopify and WMS, paste into Google Sheets, manually compare SKU counts, flag discrepancies.
verified_facts: SIG-0002 (sourced from SRC-0003, a G2/Capterra review collected 2025-03-24) describes a weekly manual reconciliation workflow between Shopify and a WMS using downloaded reports and Google Sheets.
The review claims the task consumes 4-5 hours every Monday.
The review lists consequences: stockouts, overselling, manual error risk, and delayed fulfillment.
The cluster contains exactly 1 independent source and 1 source type (review).
inferences: Estimated labor cost of ~$10-15K/year, derived from the claimed 4-5 weekly hours multiplied by an assumed loaded wage rate.

Because the signal originates on G2/Capterra, the reviewer likely already pays for adjacent software (a WMS or inventory tool) whose native reconciliation is inadequate — implying some existing budget in the category, though not for this specific solution.
The workflow is plausibly common among Shopify merchants with a separate WMS, but generalizing from one review to a population is an inference, not a finding.
assumptions: The 4-5 hour figure is accurate and not exaggerated for review effect.
The reviewer is representative of a broader merchant population rather than an edge case (e.g., unusual SKU volume or a poorly configured WMS).
A loaded ops-manager wage of $50-60/hr used in the economic impact estimate.
The canonical JTBD's 'end of the week' framing is consistent with the evidence's 'every Monday' timing (minor internal rephrasing, assumed equivalent).
unknowns: Whether any other merchant experiences this pain — there is zero corroborating evidence.

Whether existing Shopify App Store inventory-sync/reconciliation apps already solve this; the competitive landscape is entirely unaddressed by the evidence, and if mature solutions exist, willingness to pay for a new entrant collapses.
Actual dollar losses from the claimed stockouts and overselling — asserted but never quantified.
The reviewer's company size, order volume, and SKU count — pain severity likely scales with these, and no baseline is given.
The reviewer's geography and whether the claimed workflow generalizes across WMS vendors.
Whether buyers would purchase a standalone reconciliation tool or simply expect this as a feature of software they already pay for.
